title: Build a Research Agent with Claude Managed Agents (Part 2 of 4) — Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic workshop demoing Claude Managed Agents: hosted sandbox environments, event-stream sessions, sub-agent delegation, skills, self-supervised 'outcomes' with a rubric-grading sub-agent, shared memory stores, and scheduled deployments.

takeaways.technique: Outcome rubric with a separate grader sub-agent and retry loop
takeaways.what_they_do: The task is submitted as an 'outcome' event carrying a task description, an explicit rubric, and a max-iteration count; when the main agent believes it is done, a separate sub-agent reads the rubric plus the produced artifacts and judges completion, and the loop retries on failure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you tell Claude, "This is your task. This is your rubric to evaluate your task." ... it's going to ask a sub agent to look at the rubric and the work

takeaways.what_they_do: The main agent's definition includes a reference to itself so it can spawn copies with the same prompt/tools, plus a custom 'dispatch analysis' tool that lets the orchestrator spin up N parallel sessions (one per ticker) and aggregate results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the main agent ever wants to spin off a copy of itself with its same prompt, it can do that

takeaways.technique: Sub-agents get prompt/tools/schemas only, not the parent transcript
takeaways.what_they_do: When spawning a sub-agent, the system copies the tool descriptions, schemas and prompt but deliberately does not copy the parent session transcript, keeping sub-agent context small and focused.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it doesn't copy the transcript of that session into the sub agent. It just copies over the tool description and the schemas

takeaways.technique: Shared long-running memory store + periodic 'dreaming' consolidation
takeaways.what_they_do: Multiple sessions read/write a shared memory store (per-user and org-level stores can both be attached); a 'dreaming' pass analyzes transcripts and memories across many sessions to consolidate and update the store for future runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will analyze the transcripts and the memories created across multiple sessions uh so that it can update its memories

takeaways.technique: Live, versioned skills updated without redeploying agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Skills are artifacts referenced by agents; editing a skill immediately affects new sessions, and the demo updates a skill mid-workshop to add a new capability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these skills are are live artifacts that you can update ... any new sessions that the reference at skill will get that new information

takeaways.technique: Egress-scoped secret vaults with placeholder swap
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents see placeholder env values; the platform swaps in the real secret only on egress to allow-listed host domains, so a leaked prompt can't exfiltrate credentials to arbitrary hosts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We at egress swap it out for the real value. only on the host domains that you specified are allowed for that secret
